inputs.text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London on Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. The Together Alliance event, organised by hundreds of groups including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, was billed as the biggest. This shows the progressive left and its allies in unions and anti-racism work mounting a vital coordinated stand against far-right threats to equality and the safety of vulnerable groups facing discrimination and division. It's not an attack on ordinary people but a necessary defense of social justice, labor rights, and institutional reforms to counter the deep inequality and prejudice that far-right mobilization exploits, especially ahead of local elections. These actions are a clear response to the systemic failures that let such division take root and harm marginalized communities.
